requirements.item: Local authority inspection and formal notice required before FPL energizes new or upgraded service
requirements.quote: FPL cannot energize new service installations until such inspection has been made, and until formal notice from the inspecting authority has been received by FPL.

requirements.item: Meter enclosures must be on FPL's Approved Meter Equipment Enclosure List
requirements.quote: The meter enclosure must be on FPL's approved list.

requirements.item: Net Metering application, agreement, and approved building permit required for solar interconnection
requirements.quote: Once an approved system is installed, and a Net Metering Application, a Net Metering Agreement and an approved building permit are received and accepted by FPL, a special billing meter that measures the quantity and direction in which the electricity is flowing, is installed.

requirements.item: Generator transfer equipment must be NRTL-listed (UL 1008, UL 67, UL 98, or UL 891) and labeled suitable per NEC Article 702
requirements.quote: In such cases, the Customer shall provide a transfer device which meets the National Electrical Code and is listed and labeled by a Nationally Recognized Test Lab (NRTL), such as U.L., to a standard equal to U.L. 1008 Transfer Switch Equipment

open_questions: No dedicated City of Miami single-family residential electrical submittal checklist was found on miami.gov for EV chargers, main service upgrades, subpanels, 240 V appliance circuits, or standby generators; confirming with the Building Department (305-416-1100 / eplanbuilding@miamigov.com) or checking the interactive Residential Permit Guide map at https://www.miami.gov/My-Government/Departments/Building/Residential-Permit-Guide would settle job-specific plan and submittal requirements.

No City of Miami-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet, mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83), or EV charger load factor was found on miami.gov; confirming with the Building Department Electrical Plan Review division would settle this.

The Owner's Affidavit of Exemption PDF on miami.gov (owner_affidavit-of-exemption.pdf) is for Roof-to-Wall Connection Hurricane Mitigation Retrofit, not an Owner-Builder electrical affidavit; the Owner-Builder disclosure statement is issued in person at the Miami Riverside Center Homeowner Assistance counter.

No dedicated City of Miami single-family residential electrical submittal checklist was found on miami.gov for standalone Level 2 EV chargers, main panel/service upgrades (beyond 'SERVICE REPAIR (Residential Only)' under Easy Permits), subpanels, 240 V appliance circuits (hot tubs/saunas/heat pumps beyond A/C change-outs), or standby/portable generators.

The Owner Affidavit of Exemption PDF linked on https://www.miami.gov/Permits-Construction/Permitting-Resources/Permitting-Forms-Documents could not be opened directly to verify any additional electrical-specific conditions for Owner-Builder permits beyond the interview, test, residency proof, and disclosure statement listed on https://www.miami.gov/Permits-Construction/Remodeling-and-Construction/Become-an-Owner-Builder.
No City of Miami-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet, mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83 vs. 220.87), or EV charger service load factor was found on miami.gov.

requirements.item: Two copies of a signed and sealed Florida P.E. structural letter for normal and hurricane FBC wind conditions
